headline: A 2015 law requires the Department of Homeland Security to report on and plan for reducing duplicate computer systems.
what_it_does: The law directs the Chief Information Officer of the Department of Homeland Security to count how many information technology systems the department runs. It requires a count of systems that overlap, meaning two or more systems that do similar work for similar users. The officer must also produce a plan to reduce that overlap, including an estimate of possible cost savings. The plan must include a method for deciding which overlapping system should be eliminated.

who_it_affects.group: Department of Homeland Security employees and its IT staff
who_it_affects.how: They must help gather system data and prepare the required report on duplicate systems.

who_it_affects.group: Users of overlapping DHS computer systems
who_it_affects.how: Systems they use could be consolidated or retired if the department adopts the required reduction plan.
The law requires the department to estimate potential cost savings from reducing duplicate systems, but the summary does not say whether any savings will be realized.

when_it_takes_effect: Enacted August 6, 2015. The summary does not list specific reporting deadlines or implementation dates.
